text:
nina: spotted a gap in EU-prod aggregates for 2026-02-28 21:00-21:30. Looks like late ingestion from kafka partition p12 landed after the hourly recompute. Volume ~3.5k events. dashboards show counts ~30% low for a couple tenants.
omar: can you dump the sample keys? if it's bounded we should target a narrow shard run.
nina: sample keys: tenant=eu-prod, shard=s12, event_ids: [e8791..e8820] (pasted as link). job candidate: replay-2026-02-28-eu-21.
julia: curious whether this is in the "stale events" dedupe window. last policy TTL was 24h; these are within 4h late so should be fine. but recompute pipeline's dedupe step can sometimes drop if order mismatches. we should dry-run to ensure we don't double-count.
ben: suggested flags: --slice-size 400 --max-concurrency 3 --dedupe-strict true --kv-prefetch true --priority manual-burst. small enough to not disturb quota but still fast.
nina: console shows backlog: 9 queued, normal slot usage ~60%. if we bump priority it'll preempt fair-share lanes. can we limit time window to only that 30m?
omar: yes the replay system supports --start-ts and --end-ts. use --start 1709154000 --end 1709155800.
telemetry-bot: Replay job created: replay-2026-02-28-eu-21 at 1750004300. Estimated default runtime: 22m.
julia: run dry-run first: --limit 2-slices. Also capture ordering hashes.
ben: i'll carve a temporary UI quick-action in the console: "emergency recompute (slice-mode)" which wires the flags and applies an audit note. i'll open a PR but can patch infra-side now for ops.
nina: doing dry-run now.
telemetry-bot: Dry-run completed: 2 slices validated. ordering-hash mismatch for 1 slice -> flagged. Potential conflict: an in-flight consumer retry for partition p12 may reorder items.
omar: that's concerning. if ordering mismatch exists we must broaden the recompute window or rehydrate raw partition ordering. alternatively run idempotent merge strategy to reconcile without duplicating.
julia: propose: run targeted recompute with dedupe-relaxed=true and post-merge verification against downstream counts; then run a quick reconcile job that checks duplicates and fixes totals. This avoids blocking live system while we chase perfect ordering.
ben: note on quotas: we have a reserved "ops-burst" of 150 slot-minutes per week for emergency runs. Currently 90 used. this job estimated 12 slot-minutes. approve?
nina: approve. tagging run "eu-21-emergency" and annotating console.
telemetry-bot: Job started: replay-2026-02-28-eu-21 status=RUNNING. queue pos=1.
ben: watching ; will force prefix cache eviction after job success.
telemetry-bot: Job update: 50% slices processed, KV prefetch hit-rate improved to 88%.
omar: good sign. monitor downstream aggregator commit latencies.
telemetry-bot: Job completed: status=SUCCESS. recomputed aggregates +340 events. downstream commit latency spike to 1.3s for 2m while writes flushed.
julia: verify downstream totals and validate no dupes: run validation script now.
telemetry-bot: Validation: counts matched expected targets within tolerance. duplicate-check: 0 duplicates found.
nina: excellent. after-action: ben please land the quick-action UI but gate behind audit; add a tooltip describing dedupe risks.
ben: will do, opening PR 6421.
omar: follow-up: need an automation to detect small bounded late windows and auto-surface the quick-action in console for ops oncall. filing a mini RFC.
julia: also propose an additional metric in the console: "late-lag-alert-rate" per tenant which can trigger the quick-action suggestion.
nina: noted. thanks team.
